newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Electrolux Q1 profit disappoints.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Electrolux Q1 profit disappoints.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux on Tuesday posted a 14 percent fall in earnings for the first quarter of the year and promised no relief in its depressed traditional markets.

The company posted a profit of 777 million crowns ($99.6 million) after financial items for the first three months of the year compared to the same 1996 period. It said sales rose four percent to 28.72 billion crowns.

"So far this year we have faced a very difficult market situation in Europe, with lower demand in almost all product areas," said Electrolux Managing Director Leif Johansson in a written copy of his exit speech.
Johansson, who is leaving Electrolux to take over at Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo, said the European whitegoods market shrank three percent in the first quarter of 1997.
"The North American market has however been more stable but with a slight fall in demand for white goods compared with the first quarter of last year," he added.
Johansson will be replaced by Michael Treschow, who had been chief executive of industrial engineer Atlas Copco and is known in markets as a cost-cutter with a focus on shareholder value.
Average market expectations put the first quarter profit after financial items at 910 million crowns.
The news sent the share tumbling 16 crowns or 3.4 percent to 457 crowns, but it recovered a little later in the day.
The company said it would focus on improving logistics and marketing in order to make the operation less fragmented.
Both the U.S. and European whitegoods markets, which make up the backbone of the company's sales, had contracted, it said.
The company also said lower sales volumes and a less favourable product mix hurt the group's European operations.

Several analysts said the result in the group's commercial appliances division was a disappointment. The unit posted a loss of 69 million crowns in the first three months of the year compared to a 13 million crown profit in the same 1996 period.
Sales for the commercial appliances unit edged down to 2.41 billion crowns from 2.49 billion.
Electrolux pinned some of the losses in the unit on restructuring costs.

"In commercial applicances, demand remained weak in Europe. All operations reported considerably lower operating income as a result of lower sales volumes, costs referring to investments in new markets, and ongoing restructuring," Electrolux said.
Most analysts said the result was disappointing.

"All forecasts indicated a better result than the report showed," said Foreningsbanken analyst Anna Lienhart. "Looking into the future, it's difficult to see any dramatic positive changes in Electrolux's world," she added.

"The stock has rallied in the last two months, since the end of January. It's hard to see that this is justified by the current earnings level. Perhaps expectations have been a little too high," said another Stockholm-based analyst.
Electrolux said sales in its household appliances division rose to 18.89 billion crowns from 18.03 billion a year earlier while profit edged down to 642 million crowns from 681 million.
The company said the decrease in household applicances was traceable mainly to the divestment of Husqvarna Sewing Machines.
Currency effects also had an impact, one analyst said.
"The exchange rate between Italy, where the company has a lot of its production, and Germany, where the company has a lot of sales, developed unfavourably," one analyst said.
